Subject: Quick clarification on billing mechanics for spikes above commit

Hi Vanessa / Monica,

Thanks for walking us through the Dedicated commit options earlier. Before we finalize the SOW, procurement has two quick technical billing questions that need to be called out explicitly so Legal can sign-off:

1) If our workload temporarily exceeds the reserved GPU pool (e.g., a 3-hour spike during a product launch), how is that excess metered and billed? Is it per-GPU-hour, per-minute, or rounded to the next hour?

2) Is there an automatic throttling behavior once a short-term soft-cap is reached, or will Redwood always serve and bill for the extra capacity (subject to availability)? If throttling can occur, what triggers it and what notice do we get?

Hi Sam — thanks for the clear list. Looping in Monica (Customer Success) and Aditya (Sales lead) to provide the operational details and commercial options.

High level answers up front:
- Metering granularity: we bill over-commit usage at a per-GPU-minute granularity with a 1-minute minimum increment (we do not round up to the full hour).
- Soft-cap / throttling: standard Dedicated plans include a configurable soft-cap. By default we allow a small grace buffer (10% of commit) to be consumed without throttling; beyond that, default behavior is to continue serving and invoice overage at the agreed overage rate unless the customer has a strict throttle policy enabled in their account. Throttling is only enforced when capacity exhaustion occurs and the customer has opted into an enforced throttle policy.

Options we commonly offer:
1) Burst credits — pre-purchase bundles of burst minutes at a discounted rate to cover expected spikes.
2) Pro-rata rounding — for committed increases that span a billing cycle we can offer pro-rata billing for the new commit instead of immediate full-month billing.
3) Soft-cap configuration — customers can choose: allow-serving (default), throttle-on-exhaust, or enforced-queue.

Aditya / Monica — could you confirm any commercial discounts we can apply to burst credits for EdgeScale? I flagged DEAL-4789 for review.

Thanks,

Thanks Vanessa — adding the commercial detail.

Sam / EdgeScale team — two follow-ups on pricing structure for the overage:

- Standard overage rate: overage is priced at 1.8x the committed unit rate (this captures premium for unreserved capacity). This is what you would see if you consume on-demand beyond commit.
- Burst credit discount: we can offer pre-purchased burst credit packs at 35% off the standard overage rate if purchased at contract signature, or 25% off if purchased within the first 60 days after go-live.
- Minimum billing floor: because metering is per-GPU-minute we bill exact usage, but we have a 1-minute minimum per allocation. There is no hour rounding.
- Pro-rata commit uplift: if you decide to increase commit mid-month, we can prorate the new commit so you are only charged for the partial month on the increased quantity (applies to committed GPU pool only).

Commercial ask: EdgeScale's target is to keep burst spend under 12% of total committed spend annually for budgeting. With the discount on burst credits we can get to a predictable blended rate — happy to run a blended-cost model if you share the expected spike profile.

Aditya Rao
Director, Sales Operations
Redwood Inference

Hi Sam — thanks, we put together both the contract language and a sample invoice. Answers inline and attachments included.

1) Contract clause (suggested language snippet):
"
Redwood will provide a soft-cap equal to 10% of the Customer's committed GPU pool (the "Grace Buffer"). Redwood will continue to serve requests above the Grace Buffer and invoice for over-commit usage according to the Overage Rate set forth in the Order Form, unless Customer has selected an enforced Throttle policy. Enforcement of Throttle will only occur when Redwood determines, in good faith, that serving additional requests would materially degrade availability for other committed customers. Redwood will provide Customer with at least 30 minutes notice via the Console and email prior to initiating enforced Throttle, and will make commercially reasonable efforts to restore service or provision burst capacity.
"

2) Burst credits and roll-forward: we can offer burst credits that expire after 90 days from issuance; for contract-signed purchases we will provide a 90-day roll-forward window. For credits purchased after go-live we can provide a 60-day roll-forward as a one-time concession for EdgeScale.

3) Capacity shortage fallback: committed customers are given priority over on-demand traffic. If capacity exhaustion occurs, Redwood will first attempt to allocate compatible model variants or re-route to Dedicated burst nodes in other regions (if policy permits). If capacity cannot be provisioned, Customer will either be throttled (if selected) or requests will be queued until capacity is available. We will also provide a monthly usage report and spike reconciliation to support true-ups.
